title: Chapter 103: One Survivor
html:
Inspector Lee lowered his voice, the tension returning. “Tell me exactly what’s going on.”

“It’s definitely not a murder this time. I just want to take a look at her information.”

“Are you kidding? Do you think we can hand sensitive information to a private citizen? If that’s all, I’m hanging up.”

Inspector Lee hung up, leaving Chen Ge at a loss. Before he could decide what to do next, his phone vibrated with a message. “The case files cannot be released to the public. Come by between seven and eight tonight. If your reason is serious enough, I can look through them for you.”

Chen Ge understood. Too many people were listening in the office for Inspector Lee to promise anything aloud.

“Uncle Lee, do you have any records on Mu Yang High School? What happened to force the school to close down? And why are there so many supernatural stories surrounding it?”

After a while, Inspector Lee replied. “The school was built on the site of a crematorium, so the land was cheap. No one wanted it because of the stigma. Eventually, a short, heavyset old man named Chen bought the property and built a private orphanage there.

“A few years later, Jiujiang expanded its public child-welfare system. The old man transferred every eligible child to a government-supported orphanage, but several older children remained in his care. He approached school after school on their behalf, but none would accept them.

“With no other option, he bought textbooks and taught the children himself. The local news reported the story, drawing the authorities’ attention. After some discussion, the orphanage became Mu Yang High School, and the children in the old man’s care formed its first class.”

Chen Ge had not expected such a complicated history. “Inspector Lee, can you find out how many students were in that first class?”

Twenty minutes later, Inspector Lee called. “Xiao Chen, I’m in the records room. Most of the Mu Yang High School files were transferred to the city station after the case was closed.”

“Uncle Lee, I only need to confirm one thing. Were Chen Yalin and Wang Xin members of the first class?”

“Let me check.” Pages rustled over the line. “Mu Yang High School opened with twenty-five students, all from the old man’s orphanage.”

“Twenty-five?” This number was close but not exactly the same as the number of uniforms.

“Indeed, but…” Inspector Lee hesitated. “There is only one survivor, the girl you mentioned, Wang Xin.”

“The rest of them came into some kind of accident?”

“Unfortunately. First, Chen Yalin was found hanged in her dorm room. The reason was never established. Later, the remaining twenty-three students—everyone except her roommate, Wang Xin—left on a school trip. Their bus went off the road and plunged into a reservoir. Everyone aboard, including the driver, died.”

“Twenty-five students. One survivor.” Chen Ge thought of the twenty-four uniforms and finally understood why those lingering spirits returned to the classroom. To them, it was more than a school. It was home.

“Is there anything else? If not, I have to go back to work.” Inspector Lee had already done a big favor for Chen Ge.

“One last question. Is there any way to contact the survivor?” Chen Ge was now certain that Wang Xin was the person the Pen Spirit sought.

“Wang Xin was hospitalized after Chen Yalin’s death. Later, a couple adopted her. Check the adoption registry; given how unusual her case was, a record should remain.”

After the call, Chen Ge followed Inspector Lee’s advice and searched the registry. Half an hour later, he found Wang Xin. Her adoptive mother was a woman named Madam Gu.

Madam Gu’s profile contained numerous posts asking for help. Chen Ge had intended only to learn more about her, but his expression changed as he read.

Wang Xin suffered from a serious psychological disorder, and Madam Gu had spent years seeking professional care. Eventually, a doctor named Gao agreed to help.

His profile listed his credentials: senior psychologist and tenured lecturer at Jiujiang Medical University.

Could there really be such a coincidence?Chen Ge hesitated for a moment before giving Gao Ru Xue’s father a call.

“Hello?”

“Doctor Gao, I’m Gao Ru Xue’s friend. We discussed a boy’s condition last night.”

“Has the boy’s condition stabilized?”

“I’m not sure, but I’m calling about a different case.” Chen Ge decided honesty was his best option. “Have you treated a girl named Wang Xin?”

Doctor Gao was surprised. “How do you know about that?”

“I know what caused Wang Xin’s condition, and I may be able to help her. Can you give me her address?”

“You can help her?” Doctor Gao rejected the request at once. “I’m sorry, but I cannot disclose a patient’s private information.”

“Doctor Gao, Wang Xin is suffering. As her physician, you know how badly. She must live with constant fear and nightmares. Please give me a chance to help.”

Doctor Gao remained silent for a long time, then sighed. “I’ll accompany you. Meet me at the entrance to Fang Hwa Residential Area.”

“All right. I’ll see you there.” It was the best outcome Chen Ge could have hoped for.

Forty minutes later, Chen Ge met Gao Ru Xue’s father in person. He was a fit, distinguished-looking middle-aged man. After a brief introduction, Doctor Gao led him toward one of the apartment buildings.

“Can you really solve Wang Xin’s issues?” Doctor Gao was most concerned about this.

“I know the cause of her condition, so I’d say there’s a fifty percent chance I can resolve it.”

“That is more than enough. She is an unusual patient. Antidepressants and other medication have had little effect, yet I can find no underlying disorder that explains her symptoms.”

They rode the elevator to the fourteenth floor, where an apartment door already stood open. Doctor Gao had called ahead.
